sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 1:1
items.html: The first is the expansion of the spirituality — that is, the five phases of lights called Nefesh, Ruach, Neshama, Haya, Yechida. The second is the five phases of vessels, called KHB, ZA and Malchut. And one must distinguish between them in every word of this wisdom, for there is no light without a vessel, and they are opposite to one another in all their appearances. For the order of the revelation of the vessels is from above downward: KHB, ZA and Malchut; and the order of the revelation of the lights is the opposite, from below upward: Nefesh, Ruach, Neshama, Haya, Yechida. And the lack of the lower vessels in the Partzuf causes the lack of the upper lights there, so that with even a slight forgetting of the need to recognise the oppositeness between them, the matter will at once become confused. (Chapter 1, Item 2)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 2:1
items.html: The existence of vessels begins from the time the light begins to expand from above downward, that is, from the Peh [mouth] of AK downward. Indeed, they are still not discernible; only afterwards, when the light returned from them to the Emanator and the vessels remained empty, is their coarseness discernible. (Chapter 1, Item 3)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 3:1
items.html: The expansion of the light and its departure from there cause a vessel to be made. (Chapter 1, Item 9)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 4:1
items.html: Since the measure of the magnitude of the light is drawn according to the measure of the abundance of the coarseness of the screen, the coarseness and the refinement are therefore found to be of equal importance and are discerned as being mixed one with the other, so that no difference between them can be separated out or recognised. (Chapter 6, Item 3)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 5:1
items.html: After the direct light expanded and went out from within the vessels and returned to its source, and they remained without light, their coarseness was then recognised as a discernment of lowliness and deficiency, and by this the vessels were recognised. (Chapter 6, Item 3)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 6:1
items.html: The vessels, which are the expansion of reflected light from the screen and Malchut of the Rosh [head] downward, are discerned as coarseness even before their expansion into the Guf [body]; but they are not discernible before the light has departed from within them, as above in Item 71. And when the light departed from within them, then the coarseness that had been in them while they were still in Malchut of the Rosh was recognised, and also the additional coarseness that they have now newly acquired — namely, that they remained in darkness without light, which is a discernment of judgement and a coarseness that was not in them before they expanded into the Guf. (Chapter 6, Item 3)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 7:1
items.html: For such is the meaning of the ascent of reflected light from below upward, by reason of the coupling by striking that is made there. For the meaning of “from below upward” is opposition to clothing, that “it does not bear” the light clothing in it. (Chapter 1, Item 5)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 8:1
items.html: For the matter of refining bears only upon the detaining force and the limit that are in the screen out of the coarseness included in it, which comes to it because of the clash of the surrounding light against this detaining of its, which hinders the surrounding light that wishes to expand below the screen. And the matter of the clash of the surrounding light does not bear upon the vessels at all, for they in truth long for it; rather, it is the force of the screen that separates between them. (Chapter 2, Inner Light, Item 20)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 9:1
items.html: Only a single vessel, that of Keter, was made after the departure, because the departure was all at once and in a single moment. And although we discern ten Sefirot there, this is after the likeness of a vessel whose parts are not equal. (Chapter 1, Item 10)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 10:1
items.html: Because there is here only one vessel and one departure, as above in Item 75. (Chapter 1, Item 6)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 11:1
items.html: Because they are of the discernment of from below upward, as above in Item 73. (Chapter 1, Item 7, and Inner Light, Item 50)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 12:1
items.html: In a complete level, the four phases are discerned one above the other. “Above” means refinement, and “below” means coarseness. And when the discussion concerns only the vessel of drawing in the Partzuf, the four phases are discerned as one within the other, so that the coarser a phase is, the more internal it is. (Chapter 5, Inner Light, Item 3)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 13:1
items.html: The first is the coarse light that remains after the departure, and these are for the need of the Partzuf itself. The second is the records and the sparks that remain in the said coarse light, and these are for the need of the second Partzuf that comes after it. (Chapter 2, Inner Light, Item 4)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 14:1
items.html: Because in Akudim the existence of the vessels began, and there is nothing there beyond the vessel of Malchut. But after the departure of the lights of this Partzuf, vessels were already prepared here for the need of the second Partzuf, and the vessels are thus found to precede the lights of the second Partzuf. And since in the order of the departure they emerged here from above downward — for when phase four was refined to phase three the vessel of Keter was revealed, and when phase three was refined to phase two the vessel of Hochma was revealed, and so forth — they are found to stand so in the second Partzuf as well. And in this way in all the Partzufim [pl. of Partzuf], all of which were prepared in this manner. (Chapter 6, Item 5)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 15:1
items.html: It did have a vessel for its own need, namely the coarse light that remained below after the departure of the direct light. And what is said, that it did not make a vessel, means for the need of the Nukva of Keter of the second Partzuf. For that vessel is made from the sparks that descend from the coupling made in the upper phase, and before Keter there is no discernment of coarseness at all upon which the upper light might strike. Therefore no sparks fell into the vessel of Keter, and it did not make a vessel for the second Partzuf. (Chapter 4, Inner Light, Item 9)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 16:1
items.html: Because such was the beginning of their revelation and their coming to be, for the revelation of the vessels comes through the second look and the departure. At first the vessel of Keter was revealed, through the refining from phase four to phase three; afterwards, through the refining from phase three to phase two, the vessel of the level of Hochma was revealed; and when it was refined from phase two to phase one, the vessel of Bina was revealed, and so forth. Thus the upper vessels emerged first and the lower ones emerged last. Indeed, the lights emerged and were revealed in the opposite way, for at first, in the first expansion, only the light of Nefesh emerged; and when it was refined to phase three, where the coupling is made in the Hotem [nose], the discernment of the light of Ruach emerged; and when it was refined to phase two, where the coupling is made in the Ozen [ear], the light of Neshama emerged; and when it was refined to phase one, where the coupling is made in the Einayim, the light of Haya emerged; and when it was refined to the phase of Keter, the light of Yechida emerged. Thus the lower lights emerged first and the upper ones afterwards.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 17:1
items.html: For the more refined light clothes in the more refined vessel, by reason of equivalence of form, as is known. (Chapter 6, Item 15)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 18:1
items.html: That is, the four levels that emerged at the time of the refining, as the screen came into the phases in the midst of its refining. (Chapter 2, Item 1)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 19:1
items.html: For those expansions that emerged in couplings at the time of the departure are likewise considered a departure, since such is the way of a departure — that the upper light couples with it along its way — and this is not discerned as a true expansion. It is like a man who is going out and departing from the house, who necessarily halts at the places of the steps he takes, but these are not considered halts or an interruption of his going at all, because such is the way of departing from a house. They are therefore considered reflected light and judgement. (Chapter 3, Inner Light, Item 3)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 20:1
items.html: This is for two reasons. The first, because all these levels are discerned as reflected light, as explained above in Item 85. And the second, because everything that descends below the place of the coupling is reflected light and not direct light. (Chapter 4, Inner Light, Item 2)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 21:1
items.html: Two kinds of reflected light are discerned immediately at the time of the coupling by striking. The first is the light that is rejected from expanding into the vessel of Malchut, by reason of the striking of the screen, and this reflected light is discerned as surrounding light. The second is the reflected light that is born through the shared relation of the discernment of the departure and the withdrawal of phase four from the light, which joins with the said rejected light; and it is the reflected light that ascends from below upward and clothes the ten Sefirot of direct light of the Rosh [head].

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 21:2
items.html: The third kind is the fixed reflected light in Malchut of the Rosh [head], which is made there as a source from which the lights and the vessels are bestowed and flow to the Guf [body].

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 21:3
items.html: The fourth kind is the reflected light that expands from Malchut of the Rosh downward and draws and clothes the ten Sefirot of direct light that expand with it. And this reflected light is discerned as being mixed with the direct light, and it is not recognised as a garment and a vessel, because its importance is equal to that of the direct light.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 21:4
items.html: The fifth kind is the minute illumination of direct light that is bestowed below the Tabur, which is called female light. And it too is called reflected light.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 21:5
items.html: The sixth kind is the reflected light that concludes each and every Sefira of the ten Sefirot that are from the Tabur downward, until it concludes the whole Partzuf.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 21:6
items.html: The seventh kind is the reflected light that is called coarse light, which remains below without light after the departure of the direct light. For then the coarseness in its own essence is discernible, from the aspect of what had been included in it even before it expanded from the Peh [mouth] downward.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 21:7
items.html: The eighth kind is reflected light to which a doubled coarseness was added upon its coarseness, because it remained after the departure below without light. And this darkness that it has now acquired is a new coarseness, which was not in it before it expanded from the Peh downward.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 21:8
items.html: The ninth kind is the direct light in the levels that emerge at the time of the refining, which is considered reflected light and judgement because they emerge at a time of departure.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 21:9
items.html: The tenth kind is the reflected light that descends from the illumination of the coupling in the upper phase to the vessel beneath her, which is empty of its light, and which comes into a coupling by striking with the record that is there in that vessel.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 21:10
items.html: The eleventh kind is the sparks that fall into the vessels, which were separated out from the said descending reflected light, and which prevailed over the record because the illumination of the coupling shines upon them.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 21:11
items.html: The twelfth kind is the said sparks after they have been extinguished — that is, after the illumination of the coupling has departed from the upper phase, for the record then prevails over them. (Inner Observation, Part 4, Item 7)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 22:1
items.html: The first is the self of phase four, upon which the first restriction was made, which is called Malchut.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 22:2
items.html: The second is the vessels of the Rosh [head], which are only the discernment of roots of vessels.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 22:3
items.html: The third is the vessels from the Peh [mouth] downward, which are mixed with the lights.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 22:4
items.html: The fourth is the said vessels from the Peh downward after the departure, which are recognised as coarse light.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 22:5
items.html: The fifth is vessels that are empty of their lights and have records in them.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 22:6
items.html: The sixth is vessels that are empty of their lights and have no records in them.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 22:7
items.html: The seventh is vessels that were prepared for the need of the male discernments of the second expansion.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 22:8
items.html: The eighth is vessels that were prepared for the need of the female discernments of the second expansion.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 22:9
items.html: The ninth is the vessels that are below the Tabur, which are not fit to receive direct light.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 22:10
items.html: The tenth is external vessels, for the reception of surrounding lights. (In the Inner Observation, Item 56)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 23:1
items.html: Refining from coarseness is called an ascent, and complete refining, until it becomes refined like the Emanator, is called the ascent of the lights to the Emanator, for equivalence of form joins and unites spiritual things.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 24:1
items.html: The light of Malchut — which means the screen and the reflected light included in it — when it is refined and rises to the Emanator, passes through all the Sefirot; and as it passes within them it is included from all the records that remained in them from their lights, except for the last phase. Therefore, when it reaches the Emanator, that is, Malchut of the Rosh [head], from which the coupling never ceases, it too is found included in that coupling and receives from there coarseness of from below upward, whereby the records in it are again awakened and thickened in their own coarseness, which is from above downward. And then the screen descends to its place in the Guf [body], to the place of the Chazeh [chest]; and from the Chazeh upward it brings out the ten Sefirot of the Rosh, and from the Chazeh downward it expands again into the ten Sefirot of the Guf, as at first. And this is called the second expansion, or the second Partzuf, since it differs from the first Partzuf: for the matter of the vessels of the first Partzuf is from the whole coarseness of phase four, whereas the matter of all the vessels of this second Partzuf is from the coarseness of phase three. The reason is that the screen that rose to Malchut of the Rosh included nothing of the coarseness of phase four, because she left no record after her departure. (Chapter 3, Inner Light, Item 1)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 25:1
items.html: You already know that although the whole essence of the coupling by striking is in the screen in Malchut of the Rosh [head], nevertheless all the rejection and detaining in that screen is not at all in actuality, but only in the discernment of “potential.” Therefore it is impossible to discern there any matter of inner light and surrounding light at all, for light that is limited in a vessel is called inner light, and light that is not limited in a vessel is called surrounding light. And since there is as yet neither clothing here nor rejection from phase four, whence should a discernment of inner light and surrounding light arise here? The inner light and the surrounding light are therefore found joined together in the Peh [mouth], that is, in Malchut of the Rosh. But afterwards, when the clothing and the rejection that are in the Rosh went out from “potential” into “actuality” in the Guf [body], in the screen at the Tabur — for from the screen of the Tabur upward, that is, in the first nine Sefirot of the Guf, the lights clothed in vessels, and from the screen at the Tabur downward, that is, in Malchut of the Guf, the lights were rejected and did not clothe — then inner light and surrounding light were revealed here in actuality: the lights that came into the vessels from the Tabur upward are inner light, and the light that was fit to come from the Tabur downward and was rejected from there, because of the detaining of the screen at the Tabur, is surrounding light. Therefore a striking and a clash were made between the inner light — that is, the screen and the reflected light that clothes the direct light — and the surrounding light. For the surrounding light, which began to feel here the rejecting force in the coarseness of the screen, struck and clashed against it in order to refine it and to nullify the force of limit in it, so that it too might come into the internality of the Partzuf.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 25:2
items.html: And know that here the surrounding light prevailed over the inner light, and that screen at the Tabur was refined and rose to the Peh [mouth], and there it was renewed until it brought out from itself downward a new expansion of Rosh, Toch and Sof, which is called the Partzuf AB of AK. Thus the surrounding light prevailed over the force of limitation in the screen, for it has now passed from it downward in a whole and complete Partzuf, which is called AB, as above. Understand this. (Chapter 1, Inner Light, Item 6)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 26:1
items.html: For the measure of the magnitude and the whole being of the inner light depends on the magnitude of the measure of coarseness and detaining that is in the screen, since the surrounding light is rejected and remains outside the Partzuf because of that very detaining and coarseness in the screen. Thus an abundance of coarseness is found to distance the surrounding light according to the magnitude of its measure, and to bring near and to enlarge the inner light according to the magnitude of its measure. They are therefore opposite from one extreme to the other. (ibid.)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 27:1
items.html: At first the inner light certainly prevailed, for the first nine Sefirot clothed there in the reflected light of the screen in actuality, and it even remained so after the departure, since there is no absence in spirituality, as written above. And afterwards the surrounding light prevailed over the inner light, until it refined the screen entirely and equalised its form with the Emanator — that is, with Malchut of the Rosh [head], where surrounding light and inner light are joined together (as above, Item 91) — and there it received force, until the second expansion, which is called Partzuf AB, emerged from it downward (as above, Item 91).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 28:1
items.html: At the time of the coupling in the upper phase, the reflected light that descends from there into the empty vessel is found to prevail over the record that is there. And although the record is much greater than the descending reflected light, nevertheless, since the record is from after the departure of its coupling while the descending reflected light is drawn from the illumination of the coupling, it therefore prevails over it. And afterwards, when the screen has been refined from the upper phase as well and the coupling has departed there too, the record returns and prevails over the descending reflected light — that is, over the sparks that fell into its vessel — and the record descends again to its vessel as at first and nullifies their force, until they return and are renewed afterwards in the second expansion. (Chapter 3, Inner Light, Item 80, and Chapter 4, Inner Light, Item 7)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 29:1
items.html: For there is no longer a coupling by striking in the screen after it has been refined from the phase of Keter. For even in phase one there is not sufficient coarseness there for an actual coupling by striking, but only for the descent of sparks, and all the more so above Keter. (Chapter 4, Inner Light, Item 40)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 30:1
items.html: All the Sefirot are included in the screen that rose to the Emanator, for their records are included in it as it passes through them on the way of its ascent, as above in Item 90 — except for phase four, which is not in it, because she left no record of herself. Therefore it received from the Emanator only the coarseness of phase three, whose level reaches only to Hochma. Thus with respect to the vessels the discernment of Malchut is found lacking, and with respect to the lights the light of Keter is found lacking. (Chapter 4, Inner Light, Item 50)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 31:1
items.html: The first is the first look, from which come only the roots of the lights and the vessels.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 31:2
items.html: The second is the second look, from which comes the completion of the vessels.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 31:3
items.html: The third is the striking of the inner light against the surrounding light, and from it come the ascents of the lights to the Emanator.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 31:4
items.html: The fourth is the striking of the record with the descending reflected light, and from it come the vessels for the second expansion.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 31:5
items.html: The fifth is the striking of the light of Malchut with the record; and since Malchut has no record, the striking was made with her light, which is the discernment of the refined light of the records. (In the Inner Observation, Item 2)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 32:1
items.html: Their relation is like the relation of a father to his sons: one spark from the father is drawn to the son and never departs from him. So do the records themselves pass over to the second Partzuf, which is called a son to the first Partzuf, and they become in it a part of the building and the self of the Partzuf. (Chapter 2, Item 3, and in Inner Light, Item 3)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 33:1
items.html: Because they are the remainder of the expansion of the direct light from above downward. (Chapter 2, Inner Light, Item 2)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 34:1
items.html: For these records are from direct light, as the ARI says here in Chapter 2, Item 10, and the last phase does not receive direct light at all, because of the screen upon her, as is known. (Chapter 2, Item 6)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 35:1
items.html: Because of the striking and clashing of the descending reflected light with the record, by reason of their oppositeness, the descending reflected light prevailed over the record and entered into the vessel. And the two of them cannot be in one vessel, for there are no two opposites in one subject; the record is therefore compelled to go out from there, and it rises above the vessel and shines to the vessel a minute illumination, in the secret of “Tagin [crownlets].” (Chapter 4, Inner Light, Item 7)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 36:1
items.html: The record of Keter remains in the discernment of the vessel of Keter — that is, in the coarse light that remained below, which could not rise upward together with the light of Keter, as the ARI writes (Chapter 2, Item 10). And what he writes, that Keter did not make a discernment of a vessel, refers to the need of the second expansion. (Chapter 4, Inner Light, Item 9)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 37:1
items.html: The first are the records that remain from the discernment of clothing. The second are the records from the discernment of drawing. The third are the records that are clothed in their vessels. The fourth are the records that are not clothed in their own vessels but hover above the vessel, in the secret of Tagin. The fifth are the records that returned to their vessels after they had gone out from there. The sixth are the records that are included from coarse light and refined light, with no recognition by which to distinguish between them. The seventh are the records from the discernment of the refined light alone, from which the males of the second expansion were made. The eighth are the records from the discernment of the coarse light alone, from which the vessels for the males of the second expansion were made. The ninth is the record of the light of Malchut, which is only the discernment of refined light remaining from her light; but the discernment of the coarse light in her was concealed, and no record remained of it — that is, the record from the discernment of drawing in her, of which the ARI says that Malchut left no record. The tenth are the records that were included in the screen as it passed through the Sefirot on the way of its ascent to the Emanator, and that were renewed there in a new coupling for the second expansion. The eleventh are the records that remained from the first nine Sefirot that emerged at the time of the refining of the screen. The twelfth are the records from the last phases of those said levels. (Inner Observation, Item 40)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 38:1
items.html: Although the departure was all at once and in a single moment, nevertheless, since the upper light does not cease shining even for a single moment, and since the screen necessarily comes, in the course of its refining, into the four degrees of coarseness, the upper light is therefore found coupling with it upon its coming into each and every phase. (Chapter 3, Inner Light, Item 6)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 39:1
items.html: The first is that the detaining and the limit and the coarseness come into the screen as one, and nothing at all can be discerned of the screen at a time when it is not included in coarseness, for then it does not exist at all.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 39:2
items.html: The second is the discernment of detaining in “potential” that is in the screen from Malchut of the Rosh [head].

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 39:3
items.html: The third is the discernment of detaining in “actuality” that is in the screen in Malchut of the Guf [body].

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 39:4
items.html: The fourth is the inclusion of the screen in the coarseness of the first three phases at the time of its ascent.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 39:5
items.html: The fifth is that the two operations — the rejection of the light from phase four and the clothing of the light in the first nine Sefirot — are both bound up with the screen. For just as it rejects the light from the last phase, so it binds and clothes the lights that are from her upward.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 39:6
items.html: The sixth is the coarseness of from below upward, which is renewed in the screen by reason of its ascent and its coming into Malchut of the Rosh [head].

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 39:7
items.html: The seventh is the coarseness of from above downward, which is renewed in the screen through the records that were included in it as it passed through the Sefirot of the Guf [body] at the time of its refining. (Inner Observation, Item 79)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 40:1
items.html: Limitation means clothing in vessels, measured according to the measure of the magnitude of the coarseness, neither less nor more. Therefore in the Rosh [head], where even the rejection of the screen was only in “potential,” how much more so the clothing; and there it operates only in the discernment of “potential,” and there is no revelation of limitation there at all. (Chapter 1, Item 4)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 41:1
items.html: From the time of the emergence of the lights from the Peh [mouth], from above downward, to the Tabur. And it is still not discernible until the time of the return of the lights to the Emanator. For now the existences of the clothing of the coarseness began, and the coarseness and the direct light within it were of one rank, so that there was no recognition of the one clothed as distinct from the garment, before the direct light returned to the Emanator. For then the coarseness remained below without light, and the discernment of limitation in the coarseness, and the discernment of judgment in her, became discernible. (Chapter 1, Item 4)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 42:1
items.html: For the coupling is made there by the screen, which returns the light backward and does not let it expand from itself downward. Thus the light is concluded upon that phase, and it is therefore called the last phase, or the lower phase. (Chapter 3, Inner Light, Item 6)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 43:1
items.html: See Inner Light, Chapter 6, Item 40, Sub Header, “And this.”

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 44:1
items.html: They are only reflected light without direct light, and they receive only a minute illumination from direct light, in the discernment of female light, which receives and does not bestow. And these ten Sefirot are discerned as ten discernments of conclusion, each of which concludes the Sefira that corresponds to it in the ten Sefirot of the generality of the Partzuf. (Chapter 1, Inner Light, Item 80)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 45:1
items.html: This is by reason of the inverse relation between vessels and lights. For all the deficiencies in the Partzuf, just as they touch the vessels in the lowest phase among them, so do they touch the lights in the highest phase among them: with the lack of the lowest vessel the highest light is therefore lacking, and if the two lowest vessels are lacking, this causes the lack of the two highest lights. Thus the lack of light in the vessel of Malchut shows that the light of Keter is lacking from the lights of the Partzuf, and so conversely. And the lack of light in the two lower vessels, ZA and Malchut, shows the lack of the two upper lights, Keter and Hochma, and so always. And the reason is simple: the clothing of the lights in vessels is measured by the coarseness in the screen that couples with the upper light. Therefore, when the screen rises from Malchut to ZA, which is phase three, and the coupling is made in phase three, Malchut remains without light, since the place of the coupling has risen to ZA; and the light of Keter is also lacking, since from a screen of the discernment of ZA only a level of Hochma emerges. And if the place of the coupling has risen to phase two, to Bina, then the vessel of ZA also remains without light, and you now have two lower vessels without light, and correspondingly the two upper lights, the light of Keter and the light of Hochma, will be lacking, for from the coupling made in the screen of phase two only a level of Bina emerges. And so always. (Chapter 2, Inner Light, Item 8)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 46:1
items.html: Because the screen of phase four was refined first, and therefore the level of Keter was at once concealed. But the level of Malchut emerged through the ascent of Malchut to the place of Keter, and therefore she departs last. (Chapter 6, Item 14)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 47:1
items.html: For the illumination of the upper one that reaches the lower one is considered by it to be one degree higher than its own discernment. If it is in the discernment of Nefesh, the illumination that it receives is considered by it to be the discernment of Ruach; and if it is itself the discernment of Ruach, the illumination is considered by it to be the discernment of Neshama, and so forth. And the illumination that it receives from the upper one of its upper one is considered by it to be two degrees higher than its own discernment: if it is the discernment of Nefesh, the illumination is considered by it to be Neshama; and if it is itself Ruach, the illumination is considered by it to be the discernment of Haya, and so forth. Therefore here, where ZA is the discernment of Nefesh, the illumination that it receives from Bina is considered by it to be Ruach, she being its upper one; and the illumination that it receives from the upper one of its upper one, that is, from Hochma, is considered by it to be Neshama, and so forth in this way.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 48:1
items.html: Because what is received from the Peh [mouth] is the light of Nefesh, and what is received from the Hotem [nose] is the light of Ruach, and so forth. Indeed, in the vessels it is the opposite, for the level of Keter is from the Peh, and the level of Hochma from the Hotem, and so forth. And this is the inverse relation between vessels and lights.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 49:1
items.html: For Ruach is drawn from the Hotem [nose], which is the discernment of ZA of the Rosh [head], that is, phase three; and it is known that it includes the six Sefirot HGT NHY, all of which are six parts of Ruach. (Chapter 6, Inner Light, Item 70)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 50:1
items.html: See Item 19.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 51:1
items.html: Reckoned according to their illumination, it is certain that their illumination is minute and that they are only reflected light and judgment — even though, according to the origin of those couplings, they are discerned as Ruach, Neshama, Haya and Yechida.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 52:1
items.html: In the level of phase three, where Hochma is in the vessel of Keter and Bina in the vessel of Hochma, so that she draws near to receive from only one degree below her own discernment. (Chapter 6, Item 15)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 53:1
items.html: When Malchut rose to Hochma and the coupling was made in phase one, in the Einayim. (ibid.)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 54:1
items.html: For the coarseness of phase one is very faint, and her reflected light does not reach the Guf [body].

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 55:1
items.html: Through the refining of the screen. (Chapter 5, Inner Light, Item 40)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 56:1
items.html: In the ten Sefirot of the Rosh [head], and only above the world of Nekudim. (Chapter 5, Item 7)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 57:1
items.html: See Chapter 6, Inner Light, Item 60, Sub Header, “That is.”
